design_history: The 2020-2025 results motivated the fast-base choice and calibration question. This is a retrospective comparison, not an untouched outer test for the new design. The 2026 outcomes were not used in prior reported comparisons or this new parameter selection; the short extension is descriptive, not independent replication.
endpoint_rule: origin and target endpoint both in the same evaluation period
base_forecaster: fast_fhs from unchanged ECB protocol; candidate index5, variance half-life20,250 completed scenarios,alpha39/40
update: theta_new=clip(theta+eta*(hit-beta),[-1,1]); hit=1{realized_loss>issued_scaled_VaR}; all state and projection accounting exact rational
projection: p=theta_new-(theta_old+eta*(hit-beta)); retain signed correction per matured target
forecast: Q=exp(theta)*base_VaR; E=exp(theta)*base_ES; binary64 exp/log forecasts, no interval arithmetic guarantee; require finite 0<Q<=E
lanes: primary:origin_index modulo horizon; pooled ablation:one controller per currency/horizon with delayed feedback
ordering: At index t, ingest outcome of forecast at t-h if issued, update its original lane using immutable issued forecast, then issue new forecast. Never use outcomes before target endpoint.
warmup: Initialize each controller at first eligible parent forecast; update on every subsequently matured target, without reset across reporting periods.
selection: Per currency/horizon choose lane eta and separately static theta by lowest development mean FZ0. Ordered-grid ties. Freeze both for subsequent periods; no retuning on retrospective or extension results.
stratification: yearly summaries and two predictable risk-level strata: issued unscaled fast VaR above versus at-or-below median of previous250 eligible fast VaR forecasts, excluding current value; use available preceding values during start, first origin unclassified
uncertainty: All comparisons descriptive. No iid confidence intervals, tail calibration proof, conditional coverage claim, return simulation or Aladdin performance comparison.
scope: Common scaling targets VaR breach frequency only; it preserves order and positivity but does not separately calibrate ES. Clipping invalidates an unqualified telescoping coverage bound; its residual is retained.
data_vintage: current revised ECB snapshot, assumed same-day availability, no original historical release vintages
